definition: Structuring problem solving as a tree of partial solutions explored with lookahead and backtracking, optionally guided by a value/verifier model.
details: Structuring problem solving as a tree of partial solutions explored with lookahead and backtracking, optionally guided by a value/verifier model. The prompting-era ancestor of verifier-guided test-time search.

explainer.lead: Search over reasoning structures problem solving as a tree of partial solutions explored with lookahead and backtracking, optionally guided by a value or verifier model. It matters as the prompting-era ancestor of verifier-guided test-time search.

tiers.eli5: Like working through a maze: you look ahead, step back when a path dead-ends, and pick the path that looks most promising.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to let a model explore several reasoning paths and prune dead ends rather than commit to one chain. A pitfall is that search cost grows with the tree, and a weak verifier can lead it astray.
tiers.paperLevel: Problem solving is cast as exploration of a tree of partial solutions with lookahead and backtracking, optionally scored by a value or verifier model. No formal bound is given; the approach is described as the prompting-era ancestor of verifier-guided test-time search.

explainer.example: A model generates several partial solutions to a maths problem, backtracks from branches that fail a check, and continues the most promising one.
